summary.name: Noteriv
summary.one_liner: Noteriv is a free, open-source markdown note-taking app for desktop and Android, built with Rust and Tauri, with wiki-links, a graph view, a canvas, and an MCP server for AI assistants.
use_cases: take and link markdown notes in a personal knowledge base
brainstorm and mind-map on an infinite canvas
let AI assistants like Claude or Cursor read and write notes
sync notes across devices via Git or WebDAV
summary.what_it_does: Noteriv renders markdown live as you type, including bold, italic, code, math, tables and callouts, without a separate preview. Notes can link to each other with [[wiki-links]] and be explored in an interactive force-directed graph. It includes an infinite canvas for sticky notes, drawing, images and arrows, plus a kanban board, a monthly calendar with daily notes, and SM-2 spaced repetition flashcards. A built-in MCP server exposes 22 tools so Claude, Cursor and similar assistants can search, read and append to notes. Notes are plain markdown files on the local filesystem, and sync is offered through Git, local folders or WebDAV.
notable: Built with Rust and Tauri rather than Electron, for a small native binary
MCP server with 22 tools for AI assistants like Claude and Cursor
Notes stored as plain markdown files on your own filesystem
MIT licensed with plugin extensibility and multiple themes
caveats: Mobile app is listed for Android only; no iOS version is mentioned on the page
Page does not state system requirements or details of older builds beyond a link
